name: Oberlienz
kurzbeschreibung: Historic village above Lienz, featuring the pilgrimage church Maria Luggau and breathtaking views.
text:
Overview

Oberlienz is located in the sun-drenched Isel Valley in the East Tyrolean district of Lienz, just four kilometres northwest of the district capital Lienz at an elevation of 756 metres. The municipality has around 1,490 inhabitants and extends across a varied area of 33.8 square kilometres, stretching from the riverside meadows of the Isel to the prominent peaks of the southern Schober Group. Due to its sheltered, south-facing hillside terrace at the foot of Mount Schleinitz (2,904 m), Oberlienz is affectionately known as the Sunny Village of Lienz. Alongside the main village of Oberlienz, the scenic hamlets of Oberdrum and Glanz nestle into the gentle slopes. The landscape is characterized by traditional mountain farms, blooming orchards, historic dry-stone walls made of cleared stones, and an extensive network of walking and hiking trails offering unobstructed panoramic views of the rugged Lienz Dolomites.

History

Settlement along this sunny terrace dates back to pre-Roman times. In antiquity, an important Roman connecting road ran from Aguntum through what is now the municipal territory, as evidenced by archaeological finds and milestones. The village was first documented between 1060 and 1070 under the name Luenzina. For centuries, everyday life in Oberlienz was shaped by agriculture, crafts, and the hydropower of the rushing Schleinitzbach stream. An outstanding monument of sacred architecture is the Parish Church of the Assumption of Mary: the late Gothic building preserves precious frescoes from around 1400, including the famous Mass of Saint Gregory on the exterior chancel wall. Perched high above the valley floor on a wooded moraine hill stands the Romanesque St. Helena Chapel dating from the 13th century, a landmark visible far across the Isel Valley. A major fire in 1809 during the Tyrolean struggles for freedom destroyed large parts of the village, leading to the rebuilding of farms in their present form.

Getting There

Reaching Oberlienz is very convenient thanks to its immediate proximity to Lienz. By car, visitors travel via the Felbertauern Road B108, which leads directly through the Isel Valley from Mittersill and Matrei in East Tyrol; a well-signposted exit brings you into the village centre within minutes. From the south and Carinthia, take the Drau Valley Road B100 to Lienz and proceed north onto the B108. Rail travellers arrive at Lienz main railway station on the Drau Valley Railway. From the forecourt of Lienz station, frequent regional bus lines operated by Verkehrsverbund Tirol (VVT) connect to Oberlienz and Oberdrum in around ten minutes. Cyclists can enjoy a comfortable ride along the paved Isel Valley Cycle Path R2, running parallel to the last free-flowing glacial river in the Eastern Alps.

Tips

The cultural highlight of the municipality is the Open-Air Museum Oberlienz, situated directly along the Schleinitzbach stream. This authentically restored site features a fully operational grain mill, a historic blacksmith forge, a rare water-powered wool carding workshop, and an old flax-breaking hut. Hikers should not miss the scenic walk up to St. Helena Chapel or the rewarding alpine ascent of Mount Schleinitz at 2,904 metres, which rewards climbers with panoramic vistas across the High Tauern and the Dolomites. Families will appreciate the gentle Feldgröfelweg trail, leading past centuries-old dry-stone walls. In winter, groomed winter walking trails and the immediate proximity to the Zettersfeld ski area guarantee sunny outdoor adventures.
